name: The Office
direction: Classic mid-run Scranton: Michael is regional manager and desperate for love and approval, Jim and Pam's slow-burn romance, Dwight's endless quest for power, Andy arrives from Stamford. Grounded, warm, cringe comedy with real season-long arcs and recurring side characters.

bible.theme: Everyone wants to be seen by someone: Michael by the whole office, Dwight by power, Jim by Pam, Andy by anyone who'll sing along.
bible.era: Season 2-3 energy: Jim and Pam slow burn with Roy in the way, Michael and Jan, Andy arriving from Stamford as a rival for Dwight.

arcs.name: Will They, Won't They: Jim and Pam
arcs.summary: Jim's crush on Pam grows while she is stuck with Roy's endless engagement. Small kindnesses build toward a confession.

perEpisode.beat: Jim and Pam prank Dwight together; Roy picks Pam up late and barely notices her.
Pam shows Jim her art; Jim is the only one who looks.
Roy forgets Pam's art show; Jim shows up instead.
Jim almost tells Pam, interrupted by Michael.
Pam sees Jim with another woman and is jealous, unsure why.
Jim confesses; Pam says she can't, but doesn't say she doesn't feel it. Jim requests a transfer to Stamford.

arcs.payoff: Jim confesses in the finale; Pam hesitates and Jim leaves for Stamford, a hook for season 2.

arcs.name: Michael Wants to Be Loved
arcs.summary: Michael's schemes to win affection backfire, but he sometimes earns real warmth. He also pursues Jan's approval.

perEpisode.beat: Michael throws a mandatory fun meeting; only Kevin is happy.
Jan visits and Michael oversells himself, nearly costing him credibility.
Michael's failed party leaves him alone; Darryl and Pam sit with him.
David Wallace praises Michael's sales numbers; Michael takes it badly well.
Corporate threatens downsizing; the office rallies for Michael without telling him.
Michael learns they covered for him and is truly moved.

arcs.payoff: The office shows it likes him; he hides tears in the conference room.

arcs.name: Dwight vs. Andy
arcs.summary: Andy arrives from Stamford with a better tie and a better voice, so Dwight escalates to keep his status as Michael's favorite.

perEpisode.beat: Andy arrives and sings a welcome; Dwight declares a secret war.
Dwight tests Andy's sales claims; Andy outsells him.
Dwight sabotages Andy; Jim helps by accident.
Andy and Dwight forced to share a client; they succeed by luck.
Dwight is named Assistant Regional Manager in a technicality, Andy sulks, then they share a grudging nod.

arcs.payoff: Armed truce; Dwight keeps his title, Andy keeps a crowd.

arcs.name: Angela and Dwight Secret
arcs.summary: Dwight and Angela's covert flirtation leaks in tiny hints.

perEpisode.beat: Angela defends Dwight bizarrely.
Kevin notices them leaving the same parking lot at the same time.
Oscar figures it out and keeps it to himself, annoyed.

arcs.payoff: Oscar and Kevin both know; nobody says anything.

tentpoles.plan: Michael hosts the Dundies at Chili's; Pam wins 'Whitest Sneakers', gets drunk and honest, Jim notices.
Stanley's one joy is threatened and Andy's arrival costs the office Pretzel Day, so Dwight blames him.
Michael fires someone in a costume as a bit; costume contest humiliates Dwight and Andy.
Michael makes the charity run about himself; Jim and Pam walk it together.
Offsite outing shifts the Jim/Pam dynamic as Jim brings a date.
Party Planning Committee fights; Michael's Yankee Swap gift reveals his loneliness while the office rallies for him.

bible.finale: Corporate downsizing review ends in Michael's favor because the staff vouch for him. Jim confesses to Pam, who hesitates; Jim takes the Stamford transfer. Dwight claims a title; Andy stays. Final hook: Pam's desk with a card from Jim, and Roy's wedding date finally set.
